hypotheses.justification: Only n = 0 needs a new argument. Put a = (i.2 : A). At a chart point, let P be its image prime and Q its ambient prime. The existing positive-degree proof gives a ∈ P ↔ f a ∈ Q, so a ∉ P since f a ∉ Q. Apply that proof to r*a, homogeneous of positive degree i.1. Primality and map_mul then cancel a and f a, giving r ∈ P ↔ f r ∈ Q. By mem_basicOpen this proves the required equality. Empty charts, including f a = 0, are vacuous.

The equality holds for arbitrary r. Retain the current positive-homogeneous proof as an auxiliary, obtained from degreeScaledChartSpec_preimage_basicOpen. At each chart point, its image prime P and ambient prime Q agree under f on positive homogeneous elements; multiplying degree-zero elements by i.2 and using primality extends this to degree zero. Moreover, Ideal.comap f Q is homogeneous: positivity of d and homogeneous decomposition give f (decompose 𝒜 x k) = decompose ℬ (f x) (d*k), by expanding DirectSum.sum_support_decompose and using decompose_of_mem_same/ne. This argument is also implemented in DegreeScaledMapPoint.lean. Ideal.IsHomogeneous.mem_iff therefore yields P = Ideal.comap f Q, proving the conclusion for every r by mem_basicOpen. Zero elements and empty charts require no additional assumptions. Both reported hypotheses can also be removed together.
